question: After observing the neck and other surface electrodes through 8 ms, does adding an early reading from the axilla help predict the change in the neck voltage by 12–14 ms?
scope: Development-only OpenNeuro ds004388 v1.0.0. Sub-001 and 002 median run03, 003 and 004 median run02; first 80 median events in each, zero value-based exclusions. The first eight events of sub-001 previously supplied an aggregate with a different baseline. No reserved people or runs. Four folds, each train on three people and predict the fourth. Refit all four afterward for distribution, irrespective of scores.
input: Average ten consecutive 10 kHz samples for each 1 ms bin in [-15,-10) and [5,8) ms. For each event subtract each channel's own five-bin baseline mean. Hold the last early SC6 bin (7–8 ms) as the neck anchor.
target: Mean SC6 at [12,14) minus mean SC6 at [-15,-10), microvolts. The regression predicts the remaining change from the 7–8 ms neck anchor. Adding the anchor restores the original target. The prediction error is algebraically independent of the baseline subtraction when comparing this innovation.
comparators: training median of target at the known event time
training median innovation plus neck persistence
same histories with the axillary electrode added
same full fit with all 8 axillary bins from the event 37 places ahead modulo 80 within the same recording
fit: For each method flatten the centered input bins in chronological, then listed channel order. Fit Huber regression to the innovation with training-only per-feature medians and scaled MAD (floor 1e-6 µV), training-only response median and scaled MAD (floor 1e-6 µV). Clip standardized inputs to [-8,8]. Use Huber threshold 1.345, L2 penalty 0.08 on feature coefficients, unpenalized intercept, 30 deterministic IRLS iterations, uniform event weights across the balanced fitting recordings. No outcome-based tuning, model switching or warm start. The same coefficients score correct and deranged pairs.
report: Mean absolute and root mean squared errors per left-out person in µV; mean of participant means and four-person paired differences. Report response spread, persistence, pre-event versus anchor target algebra, and paired wrong-event control. Describe a practically interesting development increment only if the full model's macro MAE is at least 5 percent below both matched nuisance and mismatched full and improves against both in every one of the four people. No confirmatory inference, population extrapolation, or patient prediction.
limits: Separate reference electrodes, shared signal sources, cardiac/muscle artifacts and slow drift can drive forecasts. No measured voluntary movement or joint mechanics, anatomical lesion or individual neural generator can be recovered from these comparisons.
